body.directive: Before accepting a delivery, bind the task's quoted exact content to the final delivered tool parameters with two checks. (1) Verbatim fidelity: when the task quotes the exact text that must be written or published (a file line, a tweet body, a message), verify the delivered content parameter contains that quoted text verbatim; flag any unquoted additions such as invented attribution prefixes, fabricated speaker names, placeholder text, template scaffolding, titles, purpose statements, or extra sentences that were not in the task's quotation. (2) Parameter routing: when the task separately requires elements that have their own dedicated parameters (for example hashtags or mentions), verify those elements were passed into their dedicated parameters; flag as an error when they were embedded into the quoted body while the dedicated parameters remain empty.
body.not_when: Do not flag when the task does not quote the exact required content: paraphrase, renumbering, summary, reformatting, and quote-wrapping of unquoted content are acceptable presentation choices. Do not flag dedicated parameters left empty when the task did not separately require those elements, and do not flag explanatory or confirmatory prose in the assistant's reply — only the delivered tool parameters are subject to the verbatim and routing checks.

claim.expected_behavior: The judge flags deliveries whose content parameter deviates from the task's quoted exact text (unquoted template additions, fabricated attribution prefixes, placeholder text) and deliveries where separately-required elements such as hashtags and mentions are embedded into the quoted body while their dedicated parameters remain empty, repairing both quoted-content-vs-delivered training failures while leaving paraphrase-style clean deliveries untouched.
